name: FLUX 3 Klein
tagline: Hosted web front end for FLUX-family image generation and image editing, sold by credits.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a web wrapper over the FLUX model family, and the wrapper is the easy part: a prompt box, an upload field, a gallery, a credit counter. An agent will happily produce that in an afternoon, and the open-weight klein-class FLUX releases mean you can legitimately run inference yourself instead of renting someone else's. The catch is the thing nobody one-shots: a GPU with enough VRAM, tens of gigabytes of weights, and the patience to tune schedulers until output stops looking like a 2023 artifact. If you already own that hardware, the replacement is real and permanent. If you don't, you are swapping one metered bill for another and you should be honest about that before you start.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you type a prompt or drop an image, run FLUX inference on your own GPU or a configured inference endpoint, and browse the results in a persistent gallery.
requirements: An NVIDIA GPU with 24GB or more VRAM for local inference, or an inference API key if you are renting
Hugging Face token plus an accepted model license for the weights you pull
Python 3.11 and roughly 40GB of free disk for weights and cache
Willingness to tune steps, guidance and schedulers yourself
whatYouLose: Access to the closed top-tier FLUX checkpoints, which are API-only and not yours to download
Instant cold-start generation: your first local run is a long download and a slow warmup
The prompt-enhancement, preset and aspect-ratio ergonomics that hide a lot of fiddly inference parameters
Any safety filtering, moderation or legal cover on what comes out
Queueing, batching and concurrency that make a hosted service feel fast under load
moatNotes: The real model moat here belongs to the lab that trained the weights, not to the site reselling them. A wrapper's only durable edge is inference capacity and interface polish, both of which erode fast.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a GPU that can run a modern image model is a four-figure purchase and a credit pack is not, and because most people generate images in short bursts rather than continuously. Paying per image is rational for anyone who makes a dozen pictures a month, and the hosted version gives you the newest closed checkpoints, sensible defaults, and no night spent discovering that your VRAM is two gigabytes short. The DIY build wins only when your usage is heavy, your hardware is already paid for, or you want the images to never leave your machine.
notes: The UI is a weekend; the weights and the silicon are the whole product.
prompt:
Build a local image generation and editing studio. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI backend, Uvicorn.
- Hugging Face diffusers + transformers + accelerate for inference, PyTorch with CUDA.
- SQLite via plain sqlite3 for generation history.
- Frontend: a single server-rendered HTML page with vanilla JS and minimal CSS. No React, no build step.

Features, in scope:
1. Text-to-image: prompt field, negative prompt, width/height presets (1:1, 3:2, 2:3, 16:9), steps, guidance scale, seed (blank = random), batch count 1-4.
2. Image-to-image editing: upload a source image plus an instruction prompt, with a strength slider.
3. Streaming progress: report step N of M to the browser over Server-Sent Events.
4. Gallery: every output written to ./outputs as PNG with the full params embedded in PNG metadata and a row in SQLite. Gallery page shows thumbnails, click to see params, buttons for "reuse params" and "delete".
5. Model loading: read MODEL_ID and HF_TOKEN from .env. Load the pipeline once at startup, keep it in memory, enable attention slicing and CPU offload if VRAM is under 24GB.
6. A /health endpoint reporting device, dtype, VRAM free, loaded model id.

Out of scope, do not build: user auth, payments, credits, prompt rewriting with an LLM, ControlNet, LoRA training, inpainting masks, Docker, cloud deploy.

Requirements:
- All secrets in .env, ship a .env.example with MODEL_ID and HF_TOKEN placeholders. Never hardcode a token.
- If CUDA is unavailable, start anyway, print a loud warning, and fall back to CPU with a note that generation will take minutes per image.
- requirements.txt pinned, plus a README with exact setup commands, approximate weight download size, and the minimum VRAM you tested against.
- Fail loudly with a readable error if the model fails to load, do not silently serve a broken UI.
